findings.title: RSS/feed HTML is stored and rendered without any sanitization (stored XSS)
findings.body: poll_feed takes the raw HTML from each feed item (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and passes it to TopicEmbed.import, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Post#cook (app/models/post.rb) returns `raw` verbatim for raw_html posts, skipping the entire rendering and sanitization pipeline, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (the main app also serves cooked HTML to clients). Nothing ever sanitizes this content, so a feed entry containing `<script>` or event-handler attributes becomes stored XSS executed for every forum visitor and embed viewer. The forum trusts the configured feed URL, but a compromised or hostile blog feed would fully compromise the forum. The imported HTML should be run through Sanitize (already a dependency) before being stored.

findings.title: i.content is nil for feeds without content:encoded, crashing the hourly job
findings.body: SimpleRSS only populates `item.content` when the feed entry has a `<content:encoded>` (or `<content>`) element. Plain RSS 2.0 feeds that only provide `<description>` — which is extremely common — will have `i.content == nil`, so `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError. The exception aborts the whole PollFeed run (and since it is raised inside the hourly scheduled job, every subsequent run fails the same way), so no topics are ever imported from such feeds. The code should fall back to `i.description` when `i.content` is blank.

findings.title: Per-URL retrieval throttle is trivially bypassed, enabling unauthenticated fetch amplification
findings.body: The anonymous-accessible GET /embed/best endpoint enqueues a RetrieveTopic job for any embed_url, which makes the server perform an outbound HTTP fetch of that URL (TopicRetriever -> TopicEmbed.import_remote -> open(url)). The only protection is a 60-second Redis throttle keyed on the exact URL string (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`). An attacker can bypass it indefinitely by appending unique query strings (e.g. ?r=1, ?r=2, ...) to the same page on the embeddable host, causing the forum to hammer the configured embeddable host with unbounded fetches — a denial-of-service amplification against the very site the forum operator embeds. The throttle should be normalized (e.g. keyed on host/path, or a global rate limit) and import_remote should have timeouts and size limits.

findings.title: Editing an already-released migration to add force: true is ineffective and dangerous
findings.body: This migration was already merged and run by existing installations; changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` will never execute for anyone who already migrated, so whatever problem the edit was meant to fix silently persists for them. Worse, `force: true` drops the existing table before recreating it — for any environment where this migration has not yet run but the table exists with data, running it will destroy that data. If the table needs to be recreated, that must be done in a new migration.

findings.title: postMessage origin check accepts origins that merely start with the forum URL
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring check, not an origin comparison. If discourseUrl is 'https://forum.example.com', then a message from origin 'https://forum.example.com.evil.com' passes the check (indexOf returns 0), so any site whose origin begins with the forum's origin string can send messages to the embed script. Today the only handled message resizes the iframe, so impact is limited to layout manipulation, but the check is wrong and will silently extend to any future message types. It should compare e.origin against the parsed origin of discourseUrl exactly.

findings.title: Check-then-create race in TopicEmbed.import crashes concurrent jobs
findings.body: import looks up `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, when absent, creates the topic, post, and TopicEmbed row inside a transaction. Two RetrieveTopic jobs (or a poll plus a retrieve) for the same URL running concurrently can both see no existing embed and both try to create; the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url makes the loser's `TopicEmbed.create!` raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, rolling back the just-created topic/post and failing the Sidekiq job (with retries). The race should be handled, e.g. by rescuing RecordNotUnique and re-reading the existing embed.

findings.title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` start with '/', so they match the `href.start_with?('/')` branch and are rewritten to `http://<feed host>//cdn.example.com/img.png`, which is broken. Protocol-relative hrefs and srcs are common in feed content; they will all 404 after import. The rewrite should skip values starting with '//'.

findings.title: Adding a column with a default rewrites and locks the posts table
findings.body: `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` on PostgreSQL versions prior to 11 rewrites the entire posts table to materialize the default, taking an access-exclusive lock for the duration. On a large forum this can block all reads/writes to posts for a long time during deploy. The safer pattern for that era is to add the column without a default, backfill in batches, then set the default and NOT NULL constraint.

findings.title: setnx + expire is not atomic; a crash between them permanently blocks retrieval of the URL
findings.body: retrieved_recently? does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` as two separate commands. If the process crashes or the Redis connection drops between the two, the key is set with no TTL, and that embed URL will be treated as 'retrieved recently' forever — the topic will never be imported. A single atomic SET with EX (or setex) avoids the window.
